headline: New law lets HHS give grants for programs that teach about and help prevent child sexual abuse.
what_it_does: This law allows the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to give grants to programs that raise awareness of child sexual abuse and work to prevent it. The programs must be evidence-informed, meaning they are based on research about what works. Each grant can last up to five years. The Government Accountability Office must also report on how the grant money is spent.

who_it_affects.group: Organizations that run child sexual abuse awareness and prevention programs
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to apply for HHS grants lasting up to five years.
They may have access to more awareness and prevention programs paid for by these grants.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Health and Human Services
who_it_affects.how: It gains the authority to award and manage these grants.
It must prepare a report on spending under the grant program.
